note: Open blockers and technical debt. 'waiver' entries require an approver and expiry; none are approved in this archive, so none relax the gate.

entries.text: Named owners, escalation contacts and support channel are human inputs; ownership.json roles are null.

No independent review/approval exists: ADR, requirements, threat model and every acceptance gate need reviewers other than the author (the executing model and its tools are not reviewers). No code-review history exists for this archive.
Tabletop exercises (upgrade, rollback, dependency outage, security incident) and game days have not been held.
No protected release workflow or signing key: evidence bundle and release manifest are hash-chained (tamper-evident) but unsigned.
No real Kubernetes cluster was available: CRD/RBAC/Deployment were never applied; HttpKubeClient is untested against a real API server; watch streaming is polling-only.
SCH-01, INV-68, PLN-02, GAP-15 and pk_core are absent from the archive; their protocol versions are unknown and the downstream adapter is exercised only against InMemoryRuntime.
Only local micro-benchmarks over in-memory fakes were run; soak, burst, fleet-scale, profiling under load and restore drills need a real environment.
mTLS client transport and KMS/envelope encryption integration for data at rest are designed but not implemented (only principal mapping from verified SANs exists).
The original 100-item pk_core checklist gate cannot run: pk_core is absent. The 68-component gate in governance/gate.py runs instead.
No LICENSE file exists in the candidate and none was invented; licensing is an owner decision.
Spans are recorded in-process only; no OTLP exporter.

ruff 0.15.11 (incl. flake8-bandit S rules) and mypy 1.20.2 ran clean on this build (0 findings, 23 files typed); suppressions are inline with rationale. Bandit itself was not installable offline and runs only in CI; its results are not claimed.
